extracted.intended_audience: Macaulay2 package authors / developers writing documentation strings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing documentation strings (doc) for Macaulay2 packages using the SimpleDoc format, including required keywords, subsection formats, and allowed markup. Intended to produce documentation nodes consumable by document, help, and viewHelp.

rubrics_metrics.name: General structure and indentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The first line of each section contains only a keyword that specifies the purpose of that section. The keywords must all be indented to the same level, and everything else must be further indented. Lines beginning with white space followed by two hyphens are ignored and can be used for commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent indentation: keywords on a line by themselves at a common indentation level; content lines must be further indented. Use '  -- comment' style to add comments which will be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key -- key of a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: Each line in this section is evaluated as a Macaulay2 expression to yield a documentation key. If the key is a string, for instance the title of a tutorial, it must be surrounded by quotation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples for documentation keys are given in document(...,Key=>...). Keys may be expressions; string keys require quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline -- headline of a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: The body of this section should be a single line description of the node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide one concise headline line describing the node.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage -- ways to use a function in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: The lines of this section present alternative usages of the key.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List different invocation forms or signatures, one per line, to show how the function/key can be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inputs -- inputs for a function in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: The text in this section is divided into subsections, each of which corresponds to one input value. The first line of each subsection contains the name of the variable corresponding to it, a colon, and the type of the variable (e.g., s2:String). The variable name and type are both optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For optional inputs use the form Name=>Type (e.g., Precision=>ZZ). Subsequent indented lines describe the variable and may include markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs -- outputs for a function in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogous to Inputs: subsections correspond to output values; the first line names the variable and type, both optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe each output in its subsection with further indented explanatory text and possible markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences -- side-effects of a function in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: Each subsection of this section should start with the keyword Item; the text in each item may include markup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Item' to enumerate side-effects; content under each Item can be formatted with allowed markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description -- description section and its subsections
rubrics_metrics.description: The text in this section occurs in subsections with keywords: Text, Tree, Code, Pre, Example, CannedExample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed subsection keywords to structure descriptive material: prose, classification trees, code, preformatted text, examples, or pre-evaluated examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text -- prose containing markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose containing markup or tex. The text in this subsection can be separated into paragraphs with blank lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Paragraphs render as HTML

tags except when top-level markup is HypertextContainer or HypertextParagraph. LaTeX may be used for math (see html(TEX)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tree -- classify documentation nodes under headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines beginning with '-' are treated as subsection headlines and may contain Macaulay2 code or Hypertext wrapped in @...@, while lines beginning with '*' or '>' are treated as keys to a documentation node and are processed by the TOH function, producing a link followed by the headline. Links beginning with '>' are treated as subnodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use '-' for headings, '*' and '>' for keys/links. Further indentation creates further sub-classifications. Purpose is to allow classification/grouping of nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example -- examples of the usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The text in this subsection consists of lines of Macaulay2 code to be used as examples in the documentation node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example code is evaluated; output will be generated automatically and incorporated into the display.

rubrics_metrics.name: CannedExample -- pre-evaluated example results
rubrics_metrics.description: The text in this subsection consists of lines containing an interaction with Macaulay2, to be displayed as an example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want to show already-computed interactions/results rather than re-evaluating code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre -- preformatted text
rubrics_metrics.description: The text in this subsection, with common indentation removed, is wrapped with PRE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Pre for blocks that should appear verbatim/monospaced without evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code -- custom Macaulay2 code
rubrics_metrics.description: The text in this subsection, with common indentation removed, is wrapped with parentheses and evaluated; the result is spliced into the list of documentation items at the appropriate point before passing the list to document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Code for larger inline snippets whose evaluation should contribute structured items to the documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis -- prepare documentation for different usages of a function
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section with this keyword prepares a standardized synopsis similar to the SYNOPSIS template of the classic document command. The text in this section occurs in subsections with keywords Heading and BaseFunction, and may repeat Usage (required), Inputs, Outputs, Consequences, and Description once for each synopsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Heading and BaseFunction; include the required Usage and optionally other sections once per synopsis variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement -- acknowledgements listed in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgements listed in a documentation node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parsed and rendered similar to Text; use to acknowledge contributors or funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributors -- non-author contributors listed in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-author contributors listed in a documentation node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List people who contributed but are not authors; rendered like other text subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: References -- references listed in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: References listed in a documentation node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parsed and rendered similar to the Text subsection; may be used to cite papers or resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation -- package citation information
rubrics_metrics.description: Package citation information. The text in these sections is parsed and rendered similar to the Text subsection and can be used to acknowledge funding sources, collaborators, and non-author contributors, or to provide references or a preferred style citing the package in academic papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can also use Tree in the first line of this section and use the nested tree structure described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat -- warnings or limitations listed in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: Warnings or limitations listed in a documentation node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parsed and rendered similar to Text; use to inform users of potential limits of the implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SeeAlso -- cross-references to other documentation nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references to other documentation nodes. The lines in this section are parsed as in the Key section and are displayed as links to other relevant documentation nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List related keys/entries to help navigation between documentation nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subnodes -- a menu of documentation nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: The lines in this section not beginning with a colon are keys giving links to the subnodes of the current documentation node. The lines beginning with a colon are subheadings used to classify the subnodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Subnodes to arrange documentation linearly (like a book) or to present a menu of child nodes; use ':'-prefixed lines as section headings within the menu.

rubrics_metrics.name: SourceCode -- sources displayed in a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: The lines in this section are parsed as a list of functions whose source code should be displayed in the documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide function names whose source should be shown; useful for API/reference nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ExampleFiles -- data files corresponding to a documentation node
rubrics_metrics.description: Each line in this section should be the name of a file in the auxiliary files directory of the package; copies of the corresponding files will be made available in the running path of the examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place example data files in the package's auxiliary files directory and list them here so examples can access them at runtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markup and embedded code (@...@ and LaTeX)
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentation system allows using LaTeX commands for math and a pair of @ characters enclosing Macaulay2 code to be executed, yielding appropriate hypertext. Any Macaulay2 code resulting in a String or Hypertext may be used inside @...@.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LaTeX for math (e.g., $\PP^3$). For longer Macaulay2 code, prefer the Code keyword rather than embedding large blocks inside @...@.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting multiple nodes at once (Node keyword)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the least indented keyword in the documentation string s is Node, possibly occurring multiple times, multiple documentation nodes will be prepared. The text following each such keyword is handled just as by doc resulting in a separate documentation node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeated Node sections to author several documentation nodes in a single string; see SimpleDoc/doc.txt for an example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backward compatibility (multidoc synonym)
rubrics_metrics.description: For backwards compatibility, the function multidoc is also a synonym for doc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing scripts calling multidoc will continue to work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template availability (docTemplate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The variable docTemplate is a String, which can be cut and pasted into a text file, to be used as a template for writing documentation for functions and other objects in a package. The template shows the Node/Key/Headline/Usage/Inputs/Outputs/... structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use docTemplate as a starting point to ensure all recommended sections and indentation are present (shows full set of allowed keywords).
